A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same WaveletDiff paper, with 26 readable pages including Appendices A–D. Full-text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original time-series generation experiments, architectural ablations, wavelet-family comparisons and diffusion reproducibility analyses in Section 4 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons in Tables 1–2 and supplementary analyses in Tables 4, 7 and 8.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same wavelet-domain diffusion procedure, level-specific transformers, gated cross-level attention, exponential noise schedule and reconstruction/energy losses.

E1.justification: Both versions use ETTh1, ETTh2, Stocks, Exchange Rate, fMRI and EEG. Short- and long-sequence coverage and the appendix evaluation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain FourierDiffusion, Diffusion-TS, TimeGAN and SigDiffusions as comparators. Comparator membership in the ablation and reproducibility experiments is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The sequence lengths, stride-one windowing, generated-sample matching, five evaluation metrics and training configurations remain identical in Section 4 and Appendix B.

E4.justification: The wavelet-family comparison, coefficient-prediction/cross-attention/scheduling/sampling ablations, distribution visualizations and architectural/wavelet reproducibility analyses are all retained without revision.

E5.justification: Tables 1, 2, 4 and 7 retain identical ± reporting. Neither version provides different run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–8 and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains WaveletDiff's ETTh1 discriminative score of 0.005 ± 0.005.

T1.justification: The wavelet definitions, decomposition/reconstruction mathematics, diffusion and loss formulations, and DTW-JS and reproducibility-score definitions remain unchanged, including Equations 1–37 and Appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same methodological contributions, DTW-JS metric, reproducibility novelty claim and stated threefold average score advantage. The added code-access sentence introduces no scientific claim.

C2.justification: Interpretations of cross-level attention, dataset-dependent energy preservation, wavelet selection and diffusion reproducibility are identical. The hardware-comparison caveat in Appendix B.5 is also unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 provides an anonymous 4open.science code address in its Reproducibility Statement. v2 replaces that disclosure with a GitHub link to GarlicWang/WaveletDiff in the abstract. Implementation, hyperparameter, hardware and dataset-access details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and positioning relative to time-domain, Fourier-domain and earlier wavelet approaches are unchanged.

P1.justification: The code-availability sentence moves from the Reproducibility Statement to the abstract with a different address, and the arXiv version/date text updates. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The abstract addition pushes one introduction line onto page 2, while removing the old code sentence locally reflows page 10. Figures 1–12, Tables 1–8 and all appendix pages render identically.

improvement.justification: v1 already supplied code-access information; v2 changes its destination and makes it more prominent in the abstract. This limited access and presentation update leaves the methods, evidence, explanations and qualifications unchanged. The supplied PDFs therefore establish no meaningful overall quality difference.
